slot.brief: Given a function built with the greatest integer function, invert (or restrict) to determine which values are excluded from its range.

stem: Let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer not exceeding $t$. For $-3\le x<3$, the values excluded from the range of $f(x)=[x]^2+2(x-[x])$ are

verdicts.working: For each integer k=floor(x) in {-3,-2,-1,0,1,2}, f(x) ranges over [k²,k²+2). Their union is [0,3) ∪ [4,6) ∪ [9,11), so its complement is option A.

working:
Write $x=n+t$, where $n=[x]\in\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and $0\le t<1$. Then $f(x)=n^2+2t\in[n^2,n^2+2)$.\nThus the range is $[0,3)\cup[4,6)\cup[9,11)$.\nIts complement is $(-\infty,0)\cup[3,4)\cup[6,9)\cup[11,\infty)$.

solution:
Write $x=n+t$, where $n=[x]\in\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and $0\le t<1$. Then $f(x)=n^2+2t\in[n^2,n^2+2)$.
Hence the range is $[0,3)\cup[4,6)\cup[9,11)$, so the excluded values are $(-\infty,0)\cup[3,4)\cup[6,9)\cup[11,\infty)$.
